papers.title_en: GridFire: A new, open source, nuclear network for stellar structure and evolution
papers.tldr: 恒星结构和演化模拟依赖精确高效的核反应网络。GridFire作为新型开源核网络实现，聚焦于计算效率、易用性和自动物理扩展。其灵活的视图引擎允许研究人员在不修改核心代码的情况下引入领域特定物理。性能测试表明，GridFire与pynucastro和MESA的net模块相当，但显著减少了用户输入和设置工作。GridFire已以GPL v3.0开源，将集成到即将发布的4D-STAR恒星结构演化代码中。
papers.abstract_en: We present a novel nuclear network implementation, GridFire, which has been developed with a focus on efficiency, ease of use, and automatic physical extension. In this first paper we provide a detailed overview of GridFire's numerics, performance characteristics, and a comparison to pre-existing nuclear network implementations pynucastro and MESA's net module. We find that generally GridFire performs similarly to and requires significantly less user input and setup than these current generation nuclear network codes. Further, GridFire has been developed with a flexible "view" based physics engine that allowing researchers to implement domain specific physics without modifying the underlying source code. GridFire has been released under an open-source license, GPL v3.0, and will eventually be incorporated into the forthcoming 4D-STAR stellar structure evolution code.

papers.title_en: SkillVetBench: LLM-as-Judge for Multi-Dimensional Security Risk Evaluation in Open-Source LLM Agent Skills
papers.authors: Ismail Hossain, Sai Puppala, Md Jahangir Alam, Tanzim Ahad, Sajedul Talukder
papers.evidence: Hugging Face上的开源LLM代理技能安全基准
papers.tldr: 开源LLM agent技能存在安全隐患，现有代码层扫描器无法检测指令层和多agent风险。我们提出SkillVetBench，一个基于LLM-as-Judge的实时公共排行榜，使用五维风险指标SARS和CVSS v4.0分解。实验表明，LLM-as-Judge在78个恶意技能上零漏报，22个良性技能上零误报，而最佳基线SKILLSIEVE漏报15%；指令层威胁（如提示注入）检测率从89%到100%缺失。方法推动了多维度语义化安全评估，支持集成评分。
papers.abstract_en: Open-source LLM agent ecosystems are growing rapidly, yet the security of community-contributed skills - modular tool definitions that extend agent capabilities - remains largely unvetted. The gap we fill: existing scanners operate at the code layer and are structurally blind to instruction-layer and multi-agent risk - natural-language directives that hijack an agent, exfiltrate data through encoded side channels, or chain harm across pipelines - so what is needed is a semantic, multi-dimensional vetting system rather than another signature matcher. We present SKILLVETBENCH, a live public leaderboard on Hugging Face that uses an LLM-as-Judge to vet agent skills. What is new: SARS (Skill Agentic Risk Score), a five-dimensional agentic-risk metric with a principled weighted formula for instruction-following systems. What is integrated: full CVSS v4.0 vector decomposition and a ClawHub dual-view that places our LLM-generated review beside the official marketplace verdict. What is demonstrated: drawing on our companion benchmark paper [ 1], the LLM-as-Judge stage achieves zero false negatives across 78 confirmed-malicious skills and zero false positives across 22 benign controls, while the best static baseline (SKILLSIEVE) still misses 15%; for instruction-layer categories such as Prompt Injection and Memory Poisoning, conventional tools miss between 89% and 100% of threats (e.g., CODEBERT detects none of nine memory-poisoning skills). Detection rates vary from 35% to 95% across four LLM evaluators, motivating ensemble scoring in production deployments.
